sections.title: Open the saved task
sections.intro: Use the same practice project and Harness environment from lesson 2.
sections.html:
In the terminal from lesson 2, run this command to open the current briefing for your saved task.

Start from a new terminal

Change to the extracted course folder that contains practice.py. Set the absolute practice path and activate the environment you used in lesson 2. For the default course environment, run:

COURSE_WORK="$(pwd -P)"
PRACTICE="$COURSE_WORK/practice"
. .venv/bin/activate

If you used your own compatible environment, activate it in place of the last line.

Find Next useful step. For a completed build, it points you to the saved checks and reviewer findings. Copy the text under Your reply to the assistant into your conversation if you want help picking up the task.

Finish Build your first report to create a task. For a preview, read the archived 1.7.0 check summary.
presenterNotes: Use the learner's actual task directory. The generated reply identifies the task and snapshot revision.
Expect a read-only briefing. Guide the learner to its Next useful step.

sections.title: Find the information you need
sections.intro: Find the saved task, the report and your lesson notes in their respective places.
sections.html:
Task and checks
$PRACTICE/task holds the saved scope, execution and checks.
Input and result
Open $PRACTICE/project/data/activity.csv and $PRACTICE/activity-report.html.
Lesson notes
These stay in the same browser profile and site while local storage is available.
presenterNotes: Ask where the learner would find checks and report output.

sections.title: Read the current briefing
sections.intro: Check that the task and report match the project you meant to reopen.
sections.html:
1. Read Goal and Current position.
  2. Check the project, task ID and revision under Snapshot identity.
  3. Follow Next useful step. If the task path is missing, find the original practice/task folder and run the status command again.
Optional assistant prompt to locate the task

copies.label: saved-task inspection prompt
copies.text: Help me find the saved reporting task from lesson 2. Confirm its path and revision, then show me its current status and next useful step. Stop after inspection.

presenterNotes: Have the learner identify the task before discussing any follow-up work.

sections.title: Read the checks and findings
sections.intro: Use the evidence saved with this run.
sections.html:
Find probe:change and probe:final under Host checks. Read their recorded outcomes and check Reviewer findings for open concerns. The two probes exercise the same reporting tests at different points in the build.

Use the saved outcomes to decide whether to inspect the report or look into a reported problem.
presenterNotes: Read the result of each probe from the actual briefing.

check.question: A saved task is completed and its chosen checks passed. What should your return brief say?

options.text: State which checks passed, inspect remaining findings and retain the limits of that evidence.
options.feedback: A completed workflow and passing selected checks are useful evidence. They do not erase findings or establish untested behavior.

options.text: State that all possible report behavior is correct, because completed means no further concern is possible.
options.feedback: Completed describes the recorded workflow. Read its checks, findings and limits before deciding whether any further action is needed.

sections.title: Add context if it helps
sections.intro: Start with the generated briefing. Add a short note for a decision or observation that lives outside the task.
sections.html:
For example, record “Check the Orion subtotal before handing off the report” beside the task path in your project notes. The next session can then find the task and understand what you wanted to check.

Optional assistant prompt for a stopping note

For a structured note tied to a task revision, see the pause-and-return procedure.

copies.label: stopping-note prompt
copies.text: Draft a short note for this task and revision. Include the decision or observation I want to retain, its evidence and the next action. Show me the note before saving it.

presenterNotes: Use the generated reply first. Add a note only for human context the task record leaves out.

sections.title: Choose the next action
sections.intro: Use the result to decide what you need next.
sections.html:
Read the existing report to find the Orion total. If you need a report containing only Orion rows, save that idea for Make it work for your needs.

For the completed practice task, continue by checking the report against its input.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to distinguish reading an existing total from requesting a new filter.

sections.title: Record your next decision
sections.intro: Capture one next step if you want to keep it with your lesson notes.
sections.html: This optional note stays in your browser profile and site. For context you want the assistant to use later, include it with the task path in your project handoff.
presenterNotes: Accept the learner's wording. A useful note names a decision and the relevant evidence.

sections.title: Continue with the report review
sections.intro: Bring the saved briefing and the HTML report to the next lesson.
sections.html:
Keep $PRACTICE/activity-report.html and the latest briefing open. If you still need a result, return to Build your first report.

Next: Open Decide whether to trust the report.
presenterNotes: Carry the same project and task into the review lesson.
